basics.name: Said Boudjelda
basics.label: Senior Lead Backend Engineer & Software Architect
basics.summary: Backend engineer and software architect with nearly 20 years of experience, from first lines of code to leading the design of critical banking and event-streaming platforms. Specialized in distributed systems on the JVM — Java, Spring, Quarkus, and Apache Kafka — built with hexagonal, domain-driven, and event-driven architecture. Creator of Kates, an open-source platform for Kafka performance and resilience testing, and contributor to Apache Kafka, Spring Boot, and Vavr. Applies AI-assisted engineering daily, enjoys code review and coaching teams, and has run workshops and talks on Spring Boot and Neo4j.

work.name: FDJ
work.summary: Company-wide reference for event streaming, keeping production Kafka clusters robust and resolving the hardest production issues.
highlights: Design and operate a company-wide, multi-cluster, highly available event-streaming platform on Apache Kafka.
Build and maintain Kafka Connect pipelines, Kafka Streams applications, and Schema Registry governance (Avro, compatibility policies).
Automate cluster provisioning, deployment, and monitoring with Helm, GitLab CI, Docker, and Kubernetes; define SLOs, alerting, and capacity plans.
Coach development teams on event-driven design, topic modeling, and consumer performance tuning; lead architecture reviews and internal workshops.

work.name: SCIAM
work.summary: Technical lead and software architect on NEO, the rewrite of a leading French bank's core accounting system as microservices designed to last for decades.
highlights: Led technical design with domain-driven design, test-driven development, and hexagonal and event-driven architecture.
Built services with Java 21, GraalVM, Quarkus, Apache Ignite, Apache Kogito, Apache Kafka, and RocksDB.
Delivered on IBM Cloud with Docker, Kubernetes, and GitLab CI.

work.name: Capco
work.summary: Engineering manager, technical lead, and lead backend developer on a bank's Neobank project: a cloud-native rewrite of its legacy mobile and web applications on Google Cloud.
highlights: Led backend development with domain-driven design, test-driven development, CQRS, event sourcing, and hexagonal architecture.
Built services with Java 17, Spring Boot, Vavr, Apache Kafka, and Kafka Connect.
Delivered with Terraform, Argo CD, GitLab CI, and Kubernetes.

work.name: BNP Paribas
work.summary: Built F.I.R.S.T. (FileAct and InterAct Routing Secure Transport) from scratch: a system managing transactional flows between BNP Paribas partners and SWIFT over SWIFTNet.
highlights: Built a distributed, asynchronous, fault-tolerant system with automatic retry that resumes failed flows from the exact step where they stopped.
Kept a complete audit trail recording the history of every update.
Applied hexagonal architecture, SOLID principles, and the transactional outbox pattern, with functional programming in Vavr and an immutable domain model across 8 collaborating modules.
Worked with Java, Spring Boot, Spring Integration, Spring Data, MongoDB, and Testcontainers in three-week Scrum sprints.

work.name: Accuity
work.summary: Developed real-time payment screening and transaction review products.
highlights: Developed HPR, a transaction-filtering REST service for PayPal meeting an SLA under 100 ms per request, backed by a configurable pool of NGINX workers for parallel processing.
Built Continuity, a multi-module web application for reviewing and deciding on flagged transactions, with audit trail, migration, message stripping, and archiving modules.
Worked with Java, Spring Boot, Vue.js, Oracle Database, MyBatis, and Spock.

work.name: ALTI
work.summary: Delivered projects for insurance, banking, and telecom clients.
highlights: Built BPSIS, a paperless, multi-tenant, multi-brand platform for borrower insurance and pensions used by insurance brokers and distributors.
Developed an application for BNP Paribas to manage disputes over ATM transactions, handling millions of records.
Served as main developer for Djezzy's value-added services during a one-year mission, implementing USSD menus for a system serving 17 million users.
